title: Canonical tooling records + derived tooling inventory
description:
Why: beads and dcg ARE part of the substrate, but their generated files are vendor-owned and must never become canonical policy. The clean separation is that machine-state records WHAT A TOOL IS FOR and WHAT WE INTEND, and verifies the installed integration satisfies it — it does not absorb the tool's own output.

What: canonical/tooling/<tool>.md, one per substrate tool. Each record carries five fixed sections:
  Function     - what the tool does, in two or three lines
  Role         - why it is part of this substrate
  Ownership    - which paths the tool owns (VENDOR) and which we own
  Intent       - the policy we require of the installed integration
  Verification - the exact command that checks Intent, and what output counts as satisfied

v0.01 ships two records:

canonical/tooling/beads.md
  Function: durable issue tracking and shared work memory; local Dolt DB, git-backed sync.
  Role: coordination layer. The task system all resident agents share.
  Ownership: VENDOR owns CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md marker blocks, .claude/settings.json,
    .codex/*, .agents/skills/beads/**, .beads/**. We own our own marker block only.
  Verification: 'bd setup claude --check' and 'bd setup codex --check' (must be run with cwd
    inside the repo — the -C flag is ignored by --check).

canonical/tooling/dcg.md
  Function: Destructive Command Guard — a pre-execution shell hook that intercepts potentially
    destructive commands. Supports Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor,
    Hermes, OpenCode and omp.
  Role: the safety boundary BENEATH the agent harnesses. It applies regardless of which
    supported agent is operating, which is what makes agents interchangeable without
    renegotiating safety each time.
  Ownership: VENDOR owns the dcg binary, its hook registration in ~/.claude/settings.json, and
    ~/.config/dcg/**. We own the recorded intent and the verification, plus (future) a project
    .dcg.toml, which dcg treats as enforcement-only.
  Verification: 'dcg doctor' — all checks must pass and hook wiring must report exactly one
    dcg hook registered.

INVENTORY DECISION: keep versions OUT of BASELINE.md. BASELINE.md is a frozen point-in-time
capture ('Captured 2026-08-30') and it already demonstrates the failure mode — it records
dcg 0.13.9 and Claude Code 2.1.251 but has no entry for bd, because it was written twelve
minutes before 'bd init' existed. Instead: state/tooling.json, DERIVED, regenerated by ms status.
canonical/tooling/*.md says what should be true; state/tooling.json records what is true. Same
canonical-versus-derived split the rest of the substrate rests on.

Observed at time of writing (2026-08-31): bd 1.2.2, dcg 0.13.9, claude 2.1.251, codex absent.
design:
The important move is that a tooling record is not prose — it is a DECLARED CHECK. The Verification section names a command and its success condition, and ms status runs it. That is what stops these records rotting into stale documentation, which is exactly what BASELINE.md did within a day.

Both tools conveniently expose a first-class check already: 'bd setup <recipe> --check' and 'dcg doctor'. A tool with no such check does not get a hand-rolled probe; it gets a record whose Verification section says 'none available', so the gap is visible rather than papered over.
acceptance_criteria:
- canonical/tooling/beads.md and canonical/tooling/dcg.md exist, each with all five sections.
- Every path named in an Ownership section matches the ownership table in machine-state-9tw.2.
- Each Verification section names a runnable command and its success condition.
- state/tooling.json is generated, not hand-written, and BASELINE.md is left unmodified.
- No vendor-generated content is copied into canonical/.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-08-31: four records, not the two the bead specified — canonical/tooling/{beads,dcg,claude,codex}.md. The two harness records were added so ms status produces the Harnesses group from the original sketch; without them the substrate would describe its tools but not its tenants.

Each record carries the five sections (Function, Role, Ownership, Intent, Verification) plus a fenced toml block that ms status executes. Ownership sections were checked line by line against the table in machine-state-9tw.2.

ONE PROJECTOR CHANGE: ms status gained an optional 'missing' label, used when a check command cannot be executed at all. 'The tool is absent' and 'the tool's check failed' are different facts, and codex needed the distinction to report 'not installed' rather than 'unknown'.

ONE CORRECTION DURING WRITING: beads.md and claude.md initially both ran 'bd setup claude --check', reporting one fact under two names. beads.md now verifies that the tracker itself is operational (bd stats); harness integration is verified in the harness records where it belongs.

INVENTORY: state/tooling.json is generated by ms status and holds all four tools. BASELINE.md is untouched, as intended — it stays a frozen capture.

ms status output is now:
  Coordination  beads 1.2.2 operational
  Harnesses     claude 2.1.251 integration stale / codex - not installed
  Safety        dcg 0.13.9 active

Groups print in alphabetical order rather than the sketch's Coordination/Safety/Harnesses. Ordering them semantically would mean hardcoding group names in the projector, which the agent-neutral rule forbids; alphabetical is deterministic and needs no mechanism. Noted rather than fixed.

TWO REAL CONDITIONS SURFACED, both pre-existing and neither invented by this bead: the claude integration is stale (filed separately as vendor maintenance), and dcg's posture is inherited defaults (machine-state-3r1). dcg.md says outright that 'dcg doctor' passing means correctly installed, not configured as intended.

Acceptance test re-run after all changes: 11/11.

FALSIFICATION AUDIT 2026-09-01. Every check declared by a tooling record has now been proven able to fail, using selective PATH shims in a scratch copy so the live inventory was never polluted.

  beads / bd stats                 -> 'database unreachable'      (shim: bd stats exits 1)
  claude / bd setup claude --check -> 'integration stale'         (shim: bd setup exits 1)
  codex  / codex --version         -> 'present but not responding' (shim: codex on PATH, exits 3)
                                      vs 'not installed' when genuinely absent
  dcg    / dcg doctor --strict     -> 'degraded'                   (proven earlier)
  claude / wiring                  -> ** UNGUARDED **, exit 1      (proven earlier)

The codex result is the interesting one: it confirms the fail/missing distinction is real rather than decorative. A broken-but-present tool and an absent tool report differently, which is what the 'missing' key was added for.

EXIT-CODE CONTRACT, previously undocumented and now in SUBSTRATE.md section 5: only a SAFETY failure is fatal. An unguarded harness exits non-zero; a down tracker, a stale vendor integration, or an unresponsive tool are reported on their line and exit 0. Verified empirically — all three health failures exit 0, only the broken guard exits 1. The split is deliberate: an agent operating without a guard is a different class of problem from an integration that has drifted, and the stale claude integration sat for a day where reporting it was sufficient to get it fixed.

SUBSTRATE.md now also states the general rule: every check must be verified to FAIL, not merely to pass. A check that cannot fail reports green for the wrong reason — which already happened once here, when the dcg record used plain 'dcg doctor', a command that exits 0 even when its own checks fail.
close_reason: Four tooling records written with executable Verification blocks; ms status renders all three groups and generates state/tooling.json. BASELINE.md untouched.

title: Write claude and codex adapter manifests
description:
Why: the adapters are where 'interchangeable agents' stops being a slogan — two agents, two manifests, zero agent-specific code in the projector.

TARGETS ARE NOT YET DECIDABLE. The previously planned targets (./CLAUDE.md and ./AGENTS.md as render targets) are withdrawn: both files are VENDOR-owned output of 'bd setup', and pointing our projector at them would fight bd's installer. See machine-state-9tw.2, which must resolve the composition seam first.

What survives from the earlier plan, unchanged:
  link  ~/.claude/skills  from canonical/skills
This target is safe and confirmed: ~/.claude/ has no skills/ directory, and 'bd setup claude --check' shows bd's claude recipe installs only the SessionStart hook in .claude/settings.json — it does not claim ~/.claude/skills.

What this bead writes once 9tw.2 lands:
- adapters/claude.toml and adapters/codex.toml, using only the three documented keys.
- Render targets chosen from the composition seam that 9tw.2 establishes, NOT from vendor-owned files.

Codex still gets the smaller manifest: ~/.codex/ does not exist on this machine, so its only present integration surface is in-repo.
design:
Explicitly NOT touching, in v0.01: global ~/.claude/settings.json (hand-written, holds the dcg PreToolUse hook — the FOREIGN case), and every bd-owned path (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/settings.json, .codex/*, .agents/skills/beads/*) — the VENDOR case.

The projector's refusal path now has two distinct classes to refuse on, not one. That is a strengthening of the original design, not a change to it: FOREIGN (a human wrote it) and VENDOR (another installer owns it) both mean 'not ours, do not write'.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both manifests parse with tomllib and use only the three documented keys.
- No manifest target is a vendor-owned path, per the ownership table from machine-state-9tw.2.
- Every source path referenced exists in canonical/.
- ~ expands correctly; no target resolves outside the repo or ~/.claude.
- The manifests contain no logic, no conditionals, no agent-specific code paths.
notes:
TARGET CORRECTION from machine-state-9tw.2: do NOT link the ~/.claude/skills container. Link individual skill directories (~/.claude/skills/<name>) — own the smallest addressable region, never the container. Same reason bd owns .agents/skills/beads/ rather than .agents/skills/.

Render targets are now resolved: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are reachable after all, but via kind='splice' with marker 'MACHINE-STATE POLICY', never kind='render'. See the ownership table and seam decision in machine-state-9tw.2.

DELIVERED 2026-08-31: adapters/claude.toml (splice ./CLAUDE.md + link ~/.claude/skills/machine-state) and adapters/codex.toml (splice ./AGENTS.md). Three targets total.

Validated: both parse with tomllib; only the five documented keys used; every source exists; no vendor path under render or link.

Projected end to end in a scratch copy with HOME redirected to a fake home, so the real ~/.claude was never touched:
- All three targets created; ms diff exit 0; idempotent and hash-stable over three runs.
- Byte-check: everything outside our region in BOTH CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md is identical to the committed vendor file. bd's one block in CLAUDE.md and both blocks in AGENTS.md intact.
- unproject restored both vendor files to their exact committed sha and left the fake ~/.claude/skills empty.

BIDIRECTIONAL CO-TENANCY PROVEN, the result this whole design rests on: after our splice, running the vendor installers (bd setup claude, bd setup codex) on top left OUR marker block intact in both files, ms diff still reported in-sync, and bd setup claude --check reported its own integration as current. Each tool rewrites only its own region and tolerates the other's. The seam works in both directions, not just ours.
close_reason: Both manifests written, validated, and projected end to end in a sandboxed home. Bidirectional co-tenancy with bd's installers proven.

title: Acceptance test: canonical is truth, projections are derived
description:
Why: one test for the one invariant. If this passes, the substrate is real and agents are interchangeable tenants of it. If it cannot be written, the architecture is wrong.

tests/acceptance.sh — one script, one exit code, five assertions:

1. PROJECT      From a clean tree, ms project realises every target in both manifests. CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md exist and now share their common policy fragments byte-for-byte. ~/.claude/skills is a symlink into canonical/skills.
2. IDEMPOTENT   ms project again changes nothing: state/projection.json is unchanged, no file mtime-churn beyond the manifest, no temp files.
3. DRIFT        Append a line to the projected CLAUDE.md. ms diff MUST exit non-zero and name CLAUDE.md. This is the assertion the whole architecture rests on.
4. RESTORE      ms project returns CLAUDE.md to canonical byte-for-byte; the hand-edit is gone. Canonical wins, always.
5. FOREIGN      Point a scratch adapter at a pre-existing unmanaged file. ms project MUST refuse and leave the file untouched. The substrate does not clobber what it did not create.

Then ms unproject, and assert nothing managed remains outside the repo.

Assertions 3 and 5 are the load-bearing ones: they prove drift is detectable and first contact is safe. A substrate that only proves its happy path has proved nothing.
design:
No root, no network, no external service. The test must be runnable offline on this machine and on a fresh checkout.

The test restores ~/.claude to its pre-test condition regardless of outcome (trap), since it is the one target outside the repo.

Verify once during implementation that assertion 3 genuinely fails when drift detection is disabled — an assertion that cannot fail is not one.
acceptance_criteria:
- tests/acceptance.sh exits 0 on this machine, printing one line per assertion.
- Assertions 3 and 5 verified to fail when their mechanism is deliberately disabled; recorded in bead notes.
- The test leaves no scratch adapters, no drift, and ~/.claude exactly as found.
- First passing run recorded in the epic before it closes.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-08-31. FIRST PASSING RUN: 11/11 assertions, exit 0. Stable across three consecutive runs.

  1a project realises every target
  1b the HOME crossing is a symlink into canonical
  1c both harnesses receive the shared fragments byte-for-byte
  1d each vendor file is untouched outside our region
  2  a second project changes nothing
  3  drift is detected and names the file
  4  canonical wins: the edit is gone, byte-for-byte
  5  a file we never created is refused, not clobbered
  6  unproject restores the vendor files exactly and leaves nothing
  3n assertion 3 fails when drift detection is disabled
  5n assertion 5 fails when the refusal is disabled

NEGATIVE CONTROLS, as required: 3n patches inspect() so splice always reports OK, then confirms tampering goes unreported; 5n patches may_write() to return True, then confirms the foreign file IS clobbered. Both assertions therefore can fail, so passing them means something.

DEVIATION: the file is tests/acceptance.py, not tests/acceptance.sh. Python was already a hard dependency (bin/ms is Python), the assertions are byte-level comparisons that bash makes awkward, and writing them in Python avoids shell quoting hazards entirely. Substance is unchanged: one script, one exit code, five assertions plus teardown.

DESIGN CHANGE from the bead: the test is HERMETIC rather than run against the live tree with a trap. It builds a throwaway copy of the repo with HOME redirected into the sandbox, so it touches neither the real ~/.claude nor the working tree, and needs no trap to be safe. Verified after three runs: no leftover sandboxes in /tmp, ~/.claude/skills still does not exist, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md still byte-identical to HEAD, working tree carries only intended new files. The bead's criterion that ~/.claude be left exactly as found is met by never touching it.
close_reason: tests/acceptance.py written and passing 11/11, including two negative controls. Hermetic: no leftover sandboxes, real ~/.claude and working tree untouched.

title: Create canonical tree and adapter manifest schema
description:
Why: fix the layout and the manifest format before anything is written into them, so the projector and the adapters have a stable contract.

What:

canonical/policy/         agent-neutral operating rules, as numbered fragments
canonical/skills/         agent-neutral skill trees (shape follows .agents/skills/beads)
canonical/desktop/        RESERVED, empty with a .gitkeep and a README line — future home for hypr/ and noctalia/
adapters/                 one <agent>.toml per agent
state/projection.json     the projection manifest (written by the projector, tracked in git)

Adapter manifest schema — deliberately tiny, three keys per target:

  [[target]]
  kind    = "render" | "link"
  path    = destination, absolute or repo-relative
  sources = ordered list of canonical paths (render) or a single canonical dir (link)

No conditionals, no templating language, no per-agent code. If an adapter needs logic, the design is wrong.
design:
canonical/policy as ordered fragments rather than one file is what makes divergent projection possible: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md can select different fragment sets while sharing the ones that matter. This is the whole reason the two files drifted by hand.

desktop/ ships empty on purpose. An empty reserved slot proves the layout anticipated Hyprland and Noctalia; adding them later must not require moving anything.
acceptance_criteria:
- Directories exist with .gitkeep where empty; state/projection.json is gitignored-exempt (tracked).
- adapters/ contains a schema comment or README documenting exactly the three keys, with one worked example.
- No projector code and no canonical content added by this bead.
notes:
Manifest schema gains a third kind (see machine-state-9tw.3):
  kind = "render" | "link" | "splice"
splice targets need one extra key naming the marker pair, e.g.
  marker = "MACHINE-STATE POLICY"
rendered by the projector into the same BEGIN/END comment form bd uses. Still no conditionals and no per-agent logic.

Layout gains a tooling slot (see machine-state-9tw.6):
  canonical/tooling/       one <tool>.md record per substrate tool (beads, dcg)
  state/tooling.json       DERIVED inventory, regenerated by ms status — never hand-edited
Versions deliberately do NOT go in BASELINE.md: that file is a frozen capture and already
omits bd, having been written twelve minutes before bd init ran.

DELIVERED 2026-08-31. Created: canonical/{policy,policy/agents,skills,tooling}/ with .gitkeep, canonical/desktop/README.md (reservation note), adapters/README.md (schema + worked example), state/projection.json (schema 1, empty targets).

SCHEMA DECISION — a fifth key. splice targets need to know how to wrap their marker, since comment syntax differs by format (Markdown <!-- -->, TOML/shell #, Lua --). Rather than infer it from the file extension — which is exactly the content-awareness the projector is forbidden to have — the manifest states it: comment = 'html' | 'hash' | 'dash'. So: three keys on every target (kind, path, sources), plus marker and comment on splice.

SUBSTRATE.md §3 updated to match; the contract now also points at adapters/README.md for the full schema.

The worked example in adapters/README.md was verified to parse with tomllib and yield three targets (render/link/splice).

NOT created here, deliberately: bin/ (machine-state-9tw.3), tests/ (machine-state-9tw.5), any canonical policy or tooling content (machine-state-9tw.6 and later), .gitignore changes (nothing yet needs ignoring; SUBSTRATE.md §2 requires appending to it rather than rewriting when the time comes).
close_reason: Canonical tree, adapter manifest schema, and initial projection manifest created. Schema gained a fifth key (comment) for splice targets; SUBSTRATE.md updated to match. No projector code, no canonical content.

title: Write bin/ms projector (project | diff | status | unproject)
description:
Why: the one piece of executable code in v0.01. Everything else is data.

What: single Python 3.14 stdlib script, no dependencies.

  ms project    read every adapters/*.toml, realise each target, update state/projection.json
  ms diff       compare each target against what canonical would produce; exit non-zero on drift, print what differs
  ms status     one line per target: kind, path, in-sync / drifted / missing / foreign
  ms unproject  remove every target this repo owns, per the manifest; leave nothing behind

Mechanisms:
  render - concatenate ordered source fragments, write atomically (temp + os.replace in the same dir)
  link   - symlink the canonical dir at the target path

SAFETY RULE, non-negotiable: a target is written only if it is absent, or a symlink this repo owns, or byte-identical to what state/projection.json says was last projected. Anything else is FOREIGN — refuse, report, and require an explicit human decision. First contact with a hand-written file must never be a silent overwrite.

Content-agnostic: the projector concatenates and copies bytes. It must not parse markdown, lua, or toml content. tomllib is used only to read adapter manifests.
design:
tomllib is stdlib in 3.11+, so adapters can be TOML with zero dependencies.

os.replace for render keeps a reader from ever seeing a half-written CLAUDE.md. Symlink for link keeps the repo the single source of truth and makes ownership obvious to a human running ls -la.

unproject exists in v0.01 because a substrate you cannot cleanly remove is not something to install on a working machine.
acceptance_criteria:
- All four subcommands work; ms diff exits non-zero on drift and zero when clean.
- The foreign-file refusal is demonstrated: pointing an adapter at a pre-existing unmanaged file causes a refusal, not an overwrite.
- ms project run twice changes nothing the second time (idempotent, no temp files left).
- ms unproject leaves no managed target behind.
- Stdlib only; works from any cwd; contains no sudo, no network, no git invocation.
notes:
OWNERSHIP CLASSES (from machine-state-9tw.2): the safety rule now distinguishes FOREIGN (hand-written by a human) from VENDOR (owned by another tool's installer, e.g. anything bd setup emits). Both are refuse-and-report; they differ only in the remediation the projector suggests — promote to canonical, versus leave to the owning tool. 'ms status' should name the class.

THIRD MECHANISM REQUIRED (from the 9tw.2 experiment): 'splice'.

  render  whole file, we own it entirely        (files we create)
  link    symlink a canonical dir at a target   (trees)
  splice  replace the region between two literal marker strings, preserving everything outside  (files we CO-OWN with a vendor)

splice is what makes co-tenancy with bd possible without a rewrite war. It follows the convention bd itself uses and which the experiment proved bd honours: bd replaces only its own markers and left a foreign block untouched in the same file.

Content-agnosticism is preserved: splice locates two literal delimiter strings and replaces the bytes between them. It does not parse markdown, lua, or toml. That is what lets the same mechanism serve Hyprland .lua and Noctalia .toml later, since both take comment markers.

splice rules:
- If both markers are present, replace between them.
- If absent, APPEND the marked region at end of file (mirrors bd's own behaviour on a markerless file).
- Never touch a byte outside our marker pair.
- unproject removes our marker pair and its content, leaving the rest intact.
- A vendor file is therefore no longer refused outright: it is refused for render/link, permitted for splice. The VENDOR class means 'do not own the file', not 'do not touch the file'.

'ms status' gains grouped output, driven by the Verification section of each canonical/tooling/<tool>.md record. Target shape:

  Coordination
    beads   1.2.2      configured
    export             enabled
  Safety
    dcg     0.13.9     active
  Harnesses
    claude  2.1.251    integrated
    codex   —          not installed

Each line is the RESULT OF RUNNING A DECLARED CHECK, not a hardcoded string: bd setup <recipe> --check for harness integration, dcg doctor for safety, export.auto from .beads/config.yaml for export. A tool whose check cannot run reports 'unknown', never 'ok'. ms status also writes state/tooling.json.

Note the -C trap: bd setup --check ignores -C and reads the real cwd, so ms must chdir before invoking it.

1. dest() used Path.resolve(), which follows the FINAL symlink, so a freshly created link target read back as the directory it pointed at and inspect() classified it foreign / exists and is not a symlink. Now resolves the parent chain only and keeps the final component.
2. The link branch of project unlinked the existing symlink BEFORE the needs-rebuilding check, but recreated it only when status was not OK. So a second ms project DELETED the link while printing unchanged. Precisely the failure the idempotency criterion exists to catch. Unlink now happens inside the rebuild branch.

ONE DESIGN CORRECTION: splice originally appended a cosmetic blank line before our BEGIN marker. That byte lives OUTSIDE our marker pair, so unproject could not take it back and the vendor file did not round-trip. Padding removed; we now add only the newline needed to keep BEGIN on its own line. project then unproject is now byte-identical for a vendor file, verified by sha256.

Only a file that exists, has no record, AND differs is FOREIGN. splice is always permitted since it touches only our own region; that is what makes vendor files reachable.

TOOLING CONVENTION FOR machine-state-9tw.6: ms status reads a fenced toml block inside each canonical/tooling/<tool>.md, with keys group, version, version_re (optional), check, ok, fail. title: Agent-neutral machine-state substrate v0.01
description:
Goal: the shared substrate BENEATH interchangeable resident agents. The resident agents are Claude Code, Codex, and future local agents — we do not write a new agent, we write the ground they stand on.

Core architecture: this repo is the canonical source of truth. Agent-specific locations (~/.claude/, ~/.codex/, repo CLAUDE.md, later ~/.config/hypr and ~/.config/noctalia) are ADAPTERS — one-way projections of canonical state, treated as derived artifacts like build output. Never hand-edited, always regenerable, always removable.

The single invariant v0.01 must prove:
  canonical -> projection is one-way, deterministic, and drift is detectable.

If that holds, adding an agent is adding an adapter manifest, and adding managed config (Hyprland, Noctalia) is adding a canonical directory. Neither touches the projector.
design:
Grounded in probes of this machine (2026-08-31):
- CLAUDE.md (3139B) and AGENTS.md (5926B) have ALREADY DRIFTED — different inodes, different beads blocks. v0.01 repairs a real defect, not a hypothetical one.
- ~/.codex/ does not exist (Codex not installed). The codex adapter therefore targets repo-root AGENTS.md, which Codex reads per-project. Do not invent a home layout for absent software.
- ~/.claude/ has no skills/, agents/, commands/, hooks/ — projecting into it is zero-clobber.
- .agents/skills/beads/{SKILL.md,agents/openai.yaml} is already the neutral-skill + per-agent-adapter pattern. Beads shipped the precedent; follow its shape rather than inventing one.
- ~/.config/hypr (13 .lua under config/ behind hyprland.lua) and ~/.config/noctalia/config.toml are plain unversioned files, no symlinks. They are FUTURE tenants, out of v0.01.
- Omarchy is not installed. We borrow the convention — canonical tree + idempotent refresh commands — not the software.

Two projection mechanisms, and only two, so that everything later is one of them:
  render - canonical fragments composed into an agent-specific file (policy -> CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md)
  link   - a canonical tree exposed verbatim at an agent path (skills -> ~/.claude/skills)
The projector stays content-agnostic: it moves bytes and composes fragments, it never parses markdown, lua, or toml. That is what lets Hyprland and Noctalia join later without touching it.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed and the acceptance test passes: a hand-edit to any projected target is detected by 'ms diff', and 'ms project' restores it to canonical byte-for-byte.

  CANONICAL - authored by us (README.md, BASELINE.md; no policy content exists yet)
  VENDOR    - owned by another tool's installer (everything bd setup emits)
  PROJECTED - derived by bin/ms from canonical
The substrate must not fight vendor installers for files they own. This makes the projector's refusal path load-bearing rather than theoretical.

title: Acceptance test: prove the substrate works and the boundary holds
description:
Why: one test is the whole point of v0.01. If it passes, the substrate is real; if it cannot be written, the design was wrong.

What: tests/acceptance.sh — one script, one pass/fail, three assertions.

LIVENESS
  Delete state/hostwatch/latest.json, then: systemctl --user start machine-state-hostwatch.service
  Within 30s latest.json exists again, parses as JSON, has schema==1, and collected_at is within 60s of now.

CONFINEMENT (write boundary)
  Run the same unit with an override whose ExecStart attempts a write to $HOME/ms-boundary-probe.
  The write MUST fail (EROFS/EACCES) and the file must not exist afterwards.

CONFINEMENT (network boundary)
  Run the same unit with an override whose ExecStart attempts socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM).
  It MUST fail with EAFNOSUPPORT/EPERM. No DNS, no connect, nothing that needs a live network to decide.

The test cleans up its own overrides. It asserts the sandbox denies things, not merely that the happy path works — a substrate whose boundary is untested is a boundary that does not exist.
design:
Both confinement probes run through the real unit via systemd drop-in overrides, so the test exercises the shipped sandbox rather than a re-declaration of it. Probes are inline python -c one-liners; no probe scripts to leave lying around.

The test must not require network, root, or an external service, so it stays runnable on a plane.

- tests/acceptance.sh exits 0 on this machine after bin/ms-agent install, and prints one line per assertion.
- Deliberately breaking the sandbox (removing RestrictAddressFamilies) makes the test fail — verified once during implementation and recorded in bead notes.
- The test leaves no drop-in overrides, probe files, or altered unit state behind.
- Result of the first passing run is recorded in the epic before closing it.

title: Write hostwatch collector (agents/hostwatch/run.py)
description:
Why: the resident payload. Deterministic stand-in for a future agent brain; proves the write path and the sandbox without needing an LLM.

What: single-file Python 3.14 stdlib script, no imports outside the stdlib, no argparse ceremony.

Collects a deliberately tiny read-only fact set:
- timestamp (UTC, ISO-8601), hostname, kernel release
- uptime seconds (/proc/uptime)
- load average (os.getloadavg)
- memory total/available (/proc/meminfo)
- root filesystem free bytes (os.statvfs on /)
- battery percent + AC state if /sys/class/power_supply exists, else null

Writes state/hostwatch/latest.json atomically (write temp in the same dir, os.replace). Repo root resolved from the script's own path, not from cwd or an env var.

On any collection error: still write a valid document with the failing field null and an 'errors' list. The agent must never leave a half-written or missing state file.
design:
Atomic replace matters because a human or a future reader may read latest.json at any moment, including mid-run. Same-directory temp keeps the rename on one filesystem (btrfs subvolume @home).

Schema is versioned from day one: top-level 'schema': 1. Cheap now, unavoidable later.

- python3 agents/hostwatch/run.py writes a valid JSON document to state/hostwatch/latest.json.
- Document contains schema, collected_at, and every field above; missing sources yield null plus an entry in errors, never a crash.
- Script is stdlib-only and works when run from any cwd.
- Running it twice leaves exactly one state file, no temp files behind.

title: Write hardened systemd --user unit and timer
description:
Why: the sandbox IS the trust boundary. The unit file is where the permission model is actually enforced, rather than merely described.

What: systemd/machine-state-hostwatch.service (Type=oneshot) and .timer.

Service sandbox, at minimum:
  NoNewPrivileges=yes
  PrivateTmp=yes
  ProtectSystem=strict
  ProtectHome=read-only
  ReadWritePaths=/home/klaas/src/machine-state/state
  ProtectKernelTunables=yes
  ProtectControlGroups=yes
  RestrictSUIDSGID=yes
  RestrictNamespaces=yes
  LockPersonality=yes
  MemoryDenyWriteExecute=yes
  SystemCallFilter=@system-service
  RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX
  UMask=0077

Timer: OnStartupSec plus OnUnitActiveSec (15min), Persistent=false. No linger, so it only ticks inside a live session.
design:
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX is chosen over IPAddressDeny for the network boundary: it is seccomp-enforced and therefore reliable in a --user unit, whereas IPAddressDeny needs BPF cgroup delegation that user scope may not have. It also fails loudly and testably (socket(AF_INET) raises), which the acceptance test depends on.

VERIFY during implementation: that ReadWritePaths= does in fact re-open the state dir read-write underneath ProtectHome=read-only in systemd 261. If it does not, drop ProtectHome and rely on ProtectSystem=strict plus ReadWritePaths, and record the change in SUBSTRATE.md.

Also verify @system-service does not block the atomic-replace path or /proc reads.

- systemd-analyze verify passes on both units.
- systemd-analyze security scores the service and the exposure level is recorded in the bead notes.
- Timer schedule is 15 minutes, non-persistent, no linger required.
- Unit references the repo paths only; no ExecStart outside the repo.

title: Write SUBSTRATE.md — the canonical/adapter contract
description:
Why: the substrate is a set of conventions. If they are not written in one place, every future agent, adapter, and managed config re-invents them. This document is the contract the projector and every adapter implement against.

What: SUBSTRATE.md at repo root, roughly two screens, stating concrete choices:

4. DRIFT — every projection is recorded in state/projection.json with source and target hashes. A hand-edit is a detectable, reportable condition, not a merge.

title: A load-dependent flutter in the chassis, exposed by the Quiet profile
description:
NOTICED 2026-09-06, minutes after Quiet became the default (machine-state-t0u.9). The user describes it as 'almost as if an insect is flapping its wings at high speed in the body' — a flutter, not a steady tone. It was not caused by the profile change; the profile change removed the 2700/3000/3400 rpm of fan noise that had been covering it.

THE EVIDENCE, gathered by testing rather than by guessing, and it points one way:

1. PRESENT ONLY WHILE RENDERING. Absent when tabbed away from Dyson Sphere Program with the fans at exactly the same floor speed, 1800/1600/1900. Something mechanical would not care whether the game has focus.
2. SCALES WITH FRAME RATE. At 60 Hz it was 'less intense but present'. With DXVK_FRAME_RATE=30 it became 'much less' and 'less frequent'. It has never been absent.
3. NOT MECHANICAL CONTACT. Silent at 3400/3600/4400 rpm with the GPU at 12 W and 0 percent utilisation — and silent through the entire descent back to idle, so no fan speed in that sweep resonates either. That exonerates the M.2 replacement the user had recently done, which was the leading suspect.

So the excitation is electrical: the dGPU's power stage switching. Coil whine IS a physical sound — inductors and ceramic capacitors vibrating at switching frequency — so 'it sounds physical' and 'it is coil whine' are the same statement, and the user's instinct is not in conflict with the measurements.

THE OPEN HYPOTHESIS, which fits everything including the flutter quality: a small electrical vibration EXCITING SOMETHING SLIGHTLY LOOSE. Pure coil whine is usually a thin tone; a flutter suggests amplitude modulation from a part in intermittent contact — an M.2 shield, an unseated thermal pad, an unevenly torqued backplate. The user intends to remove the backplate and verify.
design:
What is already in place: DXVK_FRAME_RATE in the Steam launch options for AppID 1366540. DSP runs under Proton Experimental, so DXVK provides the limiter and nothing had to be installed. 30 reduces it substantially.

What has NOT been tried, in order of how completely it addresses the cause:

1. RUN THE GAME ON THE iGPU. This machine is Intel Arrow Lake graphics plus an RTX 5090 Max-Q in hybrid mode (gpu_mux_mode 1, dgpu_disable 0), with both Vulkan ICDs installed. A 5090 drawing 65-75 W for this game is the source of the excitation; moving the work removes it rather than reducing it. Steam launch option: DXVK_FILTER_DEVICE_NAME="Intel".
2. CAP THE dGPU CLOCKS: nvidia-smi -lgc, reverted with -rgc. Needs root and may be refused — power.limit already reads [N/A] on this GPU, so the driver is not exposing everything.
3. PHYSICAL: backplate off, listen with the game running to localise it, check the M.2 shield seating, thermal pad contact and even screw torque.

RULED OUT AS A FIX: returning to Balanced. That buys silence with noise, and does not touch the cause.

RULED OUT AS AVAILABLE: the ASUS power knobs. nv_dynamic_boost, nv_tgp and nv_temp_target all report 'unavailable' through asusctl armoury on this board.
acceptance_criteria: Either the sound is localised physically and fixed by re-seating, or it is established as coil whine from the GPU power stage and the machine is configured so it is not provoked — most likely by running this game on the iGPU. Whichever it is, canonical/tooling/asusctl.md or the steam record carries the finding, because the next person to hear a flutter on a quiet machine should not have to re-derive this chain.
notes:
FAN SPEED MODULATION IS RULED OUT, 2026-09-06 16:53, by sampling the tachometers fast enough to see it.

The user's hypothesis was the middle fan, and it was a good one: a fan hunting around a target produces exactly this flutter, and it would have fitted every earlier observation — present under load, weaker at 30 fps, absent at maximum rpm, absent at idle. The 2-second sampling used for the profile work would have missed it completely, showing the average as a flat 1900.

So it was measured at 4.8 Hz for 59.4 seconds with the sound clearly audible throughout, DSP running at 60 fps:

  cpu  1800 rpm  spread 0    one distinct value in 284 samples
  gpu  1600 rpm  spread 0    one distinct value
  mid  1899 rpm  spread 100  1900 in 281 samples, 1800 in exactly 3

The three stray readings sit at samples 4, 188 and 263 — scattered, not periodic. That is the tachometer's 100 rpm quantisation crossing a boundary, not oscillation. Two of the three fans are perfectly constant.

WHAT THIS LEAVES. Every fan explanation is now closed from the software side: not speed, not resonance at a particular rpm (silent through the whole 4400-to-idle descent), not contact (silent at 4400 with the GPU idle).

But a fan can still be a RESONATOR without being the source. A blade assembly or its housing sitting near a vibrating inductor can buzz sympathetically while its speed never changes — which would make the sound seem to come from the mid fan while the tach stays flat, and would reconcile the user's ear with every measurement taken.

THE BACKPLATE CHECK IS NOW AIMED, rather than exploratory. With the cover off and the game rendering: damp the mid fan's housing with a fingertip, then the board near the GPU inductors. If damping the housing changes the sound it is resonating; if only the coil area does, the coils are radiating through the chassis and the frame cap or the iGPU route is the whole answer.

The sampler is in the session scratchpad as fan-fast.sh — read-only, 5 Hz, all three tachometers.

title: Evaluate the official Proton Pass CLI, which this project twice said did not exist
description:
CORRECTED BY THE USER 2026-09-06. This project asserted twice — in canonical/tooling/proton-pass.md's framing and in a stored memory — that Proton Pass has no CLI, no daemon and no D-Bus service, and therefore cannot serve as a credential store for anything. The GUI observations behind that were accurate and the conclusion was not: they were evidence about the DESKTOP APP, never about the product.

Proton ships an official CLI: github.com/protonpass/pass-cli, docs at protonpass.github.io/pass-cli, announced at proton.me/blog/proton-pass-cli. It lists and reads vaults and items, injects secrets into environment variables or template files through a pass://vault/item/field URI, and integrates SSH keys with existing ssh workflows. Paid tiers only (Pass Plus, Family, Professional, bundles).

Not installed here, not in any configured repository, and not on PATH as of 2026-09-06.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CORRECTION: with a CLI, Proton Pass stops being an application this repository merely records and becomes a possible answer to questions it currently has open — machine-state-u40 (what may run unattended, and where secrets that are NOT re-derivable should live) and the ssh folder sitting in Proton Drive.
design:
Read-only first, and no install without approval.

1. Provenance, which is the deciding property here as it was for proton-drive. Distribution is a Proton-published binary — 'curl -fsSL https://proton.me/download/pass-cli/install.sh | bash' or a manual fetch from https://proton.me/download/pass-cli/versions.json — with a Homebrew tap as the only package route. Piping an installer to bash is not how anything else on this machine was installed; the manual binary plus a published checksum is the same trust-on-first-use shape as proton-drive and is the only acceptable form. Establish whether a detached signature exists.
2. Where the session goes. Unknown from the docs and it is the question that decides whether this fits the machine: Secret Service, a file, or its own store. If it lands in the login keyring it inherits everything machine-state-t0u.13 established.
3. Whether a non-interactive mode exists that does not put a long-lived credential on disk. The blog's CI/CD framing implies one; the docs read so far do not describe it.
4. Only then a canonical/tooling record and an install decision.
acceptance_criteria: The record states the CLI's provenance, its session storage measured rather than assumed, and whether an agent can use it without holding a credential that outlives the session. canonical/tooling/proton-pass.md no longer implies the product has no programmatic surface, and says what the old claim was based on.

title: Agree the local Proton Drive mirror, and record that it is not a sync
description:
Proton's CLI is not a sync client and never becomes one: no daemon, no watcher, no record of what it saw last. A scheduled download is a one-way copy with a conflict strategy — it cannot tell 'deleted here' from 'added there'. The user chose to start with that mirror rather than with rclone's bisync (a Tier 4 Beta backend over a reverse-engineered API, needing the Proton password and 2FA in rclone.conf, with no modification-time support) or with an app written against Proton's own SDK.

The mirror commits to nothing: either of the other two routes can adopt the same directory later. What it does need is a written convention, because the CLI has no opinion — 'filesystem download' takes a localFolder argument and whatever we pick is real only if it is recorded.

THE ROUTE NOT TAKEN, AND WHY IT IS NOT ABSURD: ~/.local/share/proton-drive-cli/events.json holds drive.core.lastEventId, so the SDK already tracks a remote event cursor — the primitive a sync engine needs. The CLI simply does not expose it; there is no watch or events verb in its help. The ceiling is this front-end, not Proton's API. See machine-state-t0u.6 for the TypeScript environment that route would need.
design:
One local directory per REMOTE ROOT: ~/Drive/my-files is remote /my-files. That shape leaves room for a photos tree later without renaming anything, which matters because photos are going to Immich and will want their own staging directory rather than a plain mirror.

An ALLOWLIST, not a denylist. Nothing is pulled unless it is named in the record. /my-files holds a folder called 'ssh' and a file called 'Tesla Backup Passcodes'; a blanket mirror would decrypt those onto this disk in the clear, and secrets management is a recorded non-goal (SUBSTRATE.md section 9). A denylist would include each new sensitive folder by default until someone remembered to exclude it.

CONFLICT STRATEGY IS NEVER LEFT UNSET. 'filesystem download' PROMPTS when no strategy is given, and on this machine an unanswered gcr prompt hangs the caller and is not withdrawn when the client dies (machine-state-jw9). Two named modes instead:
  stage   -f skip   -d merge   never overwrites local
  refresh -f remove -d merge   remote wins, deliberately

Every run under 'timeout', and a timeout read as 'the keyring was locked' rather than as a Drive error (machine-state-t0u.13).
acceptance_criteria: canonical/tooling/proton-drive.md states the directory, the allowlist, the two modes and the timeout rule. ~/Drive/my-files exists, and the repository tracks nothing about its contents. Dolphin shows it under Home; whether it also appears in Places is the user's call, because user-places.xbel is KDE's file.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-09-06, and the upload half was demonstrated rather than described.

~/Drive/my-files exists and is empty. ~/Drive/README.txt states in the directory itself that this is a manual mirror, what does not happen (no watching, no propagation of local deletes, no upload on edit) and the three commands with their flags. A person who finds the folder in Dolphin in a year should not have to guess.

THE ROUND TRIP, one pass, both directions:
  upload   -f skip -d merge, 67 B into /my-files -> 'Uploaded: 1 items (67 B)'
  verify   filesystem info -> type file, mediaType text/plain;charset=utf-8, directRole admin,
           creation/modification 2026-09-06T13:48:58.000Z
  download -f skip -d merge into ~/Drive/my-files -> byte-identical to the original
  trash    left /my-files, appeared in /trash — trashed is not gone, and the probe is still there

MODIFICATION TIMES ARE NOT PRESERVED, and this was measured, not assumed. The file's remote modificationTime is 13:48:58Z; the local copy landed with mtime 14:49:18 local — the moment it was written. So mtime cannot answer 'which side is newer' with the OFFICIAL client either. rclone's Proton Drive backend documents the same limit from the other side. Any future sync design has to carry its own state; there is no timestamp to lean on.

UPLOAD STRATEGY CHOSEN AND ONE REFUSED. 'upload' offers create-new-revision, rename, replace, skip. The record uses create-new-revision: it keeps the remote history. 'replace' TRASHES the remote copy before uploading the local one, on the strength of a local file whose freshness nothing has established, and is not used here.

A dcg REFUSAL, answered by narrowing rather than by widening. Writing the README with a truncating redirect into ~/Drive was blocked by core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home. The answer was 'cat file | dcg create-new ~/Drive/README.txt', which is race-free exclusive creation and refuses an existing target — exactly what the guard suggests. No allowlist entry was needed or added.

The allowlist is still EMPTY: nothing has been pulled down, because which folders come down is the user's call. /my-files/ssh and the 'Tesla Backup Passcodes' file are excluded on principle regardless.

title: Prove the altered-file path for a pacman -Qkk record without root
description:
canonical/tooling/proton-pass.md records half a falsifiability proof: 'pacman -Qkk' on an ABSENT package exits 1 (proven), but the ALTERED FILE path is untested, because every file the package owns lives under /usr and is root-owned. The record says so plainly rather than claiming a proof it does not have, and says anyone with a root shell can close it in ten seconds.

There may be a way to close it with no privilege at all and no risk to the machine, in the spirit of this repository's throwaway-copy rule: a user + mount namespace ('unshare -r -m') can bind-mount an altered copy of one packaged file over the original. The alteration is visible only inside the namespace, /usr is untouched outside it, and 'pacman -Qkk proton-pass' run inside should report the file as modified.

If it works it closes the gap for EVERY record built on 'pacman -Qkk', not just this one.
acceptance_criteria: 'pacman -Qkk proton-pass' reports an altered file inside the namespace and reports the package intact outside it, both demonstrated in the same session, with no change to any file under /usr. The proton-pass record is updated to state the proof and the method, or to state why the method does not work.
notes:
PROVEN 2026-09-06, and the method costs nothing.

'unshare -r -m' gives a private mount table, so an altered copy of a packaged file can be bind-mounted over the original INSIDE the namespace while /usr stays untouched outside it. Verified after every run: 'pacman -Qkk proton-pass' outside reports 27 total files, 0 altered files, exit 0, and the file's md5 is unchanged.

Inside, over /usr/share/applications/proton-pass.desktop:
  altered copy   -> Modification time mismatch, Size mismatch, SHA256 checksum mismatch
  pristine copy  -> no warning for that file at all (cp -p, so the mtime survives)

Same namespace, same path, only the bytes differ. That PAIR is the proof; either run alone is not, because of the trap below.

THE TRAP. 'unshare -r' maps this user to uid 0, so every file owned by real root reads as nobody: pacman reports UID and GID mismatch for all 27 and the summary says '27 altered files' in the CONTROL run too. The count is useless inside a namespace; the KINDS of warning discriminate. A user-owned copy appears as root:root inside, which is why the bind-mounted pristine file reports clean.

Exit code 1 from both inside runs — any mismatch is enough — so the 'fail' label is reachable for an altered file.

Recorded in canonical/tooling/proton-pass.md, which now states both halves of its falsifiability, and in canonical/tooling/steam.md, which drops its own 'not proven' paragraph: the check there is the same command against a different package, so repeating the bind mount would prove nothing new. proton-mail and gnome-keyring inherit the same result.
close_reason: Proven without root via a mount namespace; both records updated

title: Give this machine a Secret Service, so credentials have a native home
description:
MEASURED GAP (2026-09-05): org.freedesktop.secrets is not activatable on this machine. busctl --user call org.freedesktop.secrets ... Ping -> 'The name is not activatable'; secret-tool search -> the same; no file under /usr/share/dbus-1/services/ declares the name. kwallet 6.29.0-1.1 ships /usr/bin/ksecretd under org.kde.secretservicecompat, which claims the freedesktop name only once running, and nothing starts it — this is a Hyprland session with no keyring agent, and kwalletd6 is installed but not running.

CONSEQUENCE: the Proton Drive CLI's default credential store (keychain) cannot work, which is what surfaced this. machine-state-t0u.1 depends on it.

DECIDED: gnome-keyring, not kwallet and not password-store. It is the reference org.freedesktop.secrets implementation, it is D-Bus ACTIVATABLE (verified from the Arch file list: usr/share/dbus-1/services/org.freedesktop.secrets.service, plus usr/lib/security/pam_gnome_keyring.so and a socket-activated user unit), and it is a signed repo package (cachyos-extra-v3 1:50.0-1.1) — the same provenance class as everything else recorded here. kwallet is already installed and still did not answer, and would mean owning a session service plus an unlock dialog outside a KDE session. password-store was considered and rejected for this secret: it needs an env var set in every context including agent sessions, and a missed one means the CLI silently uses a different store.

WHY A KEYCHAIN IS THE RIGHT WEIGHT HERE: the Drive session is RE-DERIVABLE. Lose it and auth login regenerates it. A durable, portable, backed-up store is for secrets that cannot be regenerated; this is not one.

TWO INDEPENDENT STEPS, deliberately separable and separately revertible:
1. Install the package. That alone makes org.freedesktop.secrets activatable and the Drive CLI's default store work. No PAM edit, no session file, nothing projected.
2. PAM auto-unlock, OPTIONAL, only to remove the unlock prompt.

PAM IS THE RISKY HALF AND HAS A VENDOR CONFLICT. Login here is greetd 0.10.3-2.1 running noctalia-greeter-session (noctalia-greeter 1.2.1-1), password typed at the greeter, so PAM auth does run and auto-unlock is possible in principle. But /etc/pam.d/greetd has ALREADY been edited by noctalia — it added 'session required pam_systemd.so' and left /etc/pam.d/greetd.bak.noctalia.20260830145901 beside it. Anything we add to that file can be reverted by the next noctalia install or update, and would fail quietly rather than loudly. The file is also owned by the greetd package, so it takes a .pacnew on update. greetd + a custom greeter is not the mainstream pam_gnome_keyring path and auto-unlock is UNVERIFIED on this machine.
design:
Package before PAM, always: editing PAM to reference a module that is not installed is the one ordering that can hurt. Both PAM lines use 'optional', so a failure never blocks login, and the auth line must sit AFTER 'auth include system-local-login' or there is no password for it to capture.

Step 1 is reversible with pacman -R. Step 2 is reversible by restoring the file, and a root TTY should stay open while it is tested.

The record for gnome-keyring must verify the thing that was actually missing — that the bus name ANSWERS — not merely that a package is installed. A check that only asks pacman would have reported green on a machine where kwallet was installed and the Secret Service still did not exist, which is the exact false green this whole session has been about.
acceptance_criteria: org.freedesktop.secrets answers on this machine, demonstrated by a live call rather than by package presence. canonical/tooling/gnome-keyring.md verifies that, and its check is proven able to fail. The PAM step, if taken, is drafted and reviewed before it is applied, is applied as a separate explicit step by the user, and its interaction with noctalia's ownership of /etc/pam.d/greetd is recorded whether or not it is resolved. ms status stays honest throughout.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-09-06, except the PAM step, which stays drafted and untaken.

gnome-keyring 1:50.0-1.1 installed by the user. The gap is closed, demonstrated by a live call rather than by package presence: busctl --user call org.freedesktop.secrets ... Ping now exits 0, and secret-tool search answers. Before the install the same command said 'The name is not activatable'. One variable, before and after — better falsifiability evidence than any synthetic control.

ACTIVATION IS BY D-BUS, NOT SYSTEMD, and this corrected the draft. gnome-keyring-daemon.socket and .service are both INACTIVE while the name answers; the process is /usr/bin/gnome-keyring-daemon --start --foreground --components=secrets, exactly the Exec= line in /usr/share/dbus-1/services/org.freedesktop.secrets.service. The falsifiability control this bead's design proposed — systemctl --user mask gnome-keyring-daemon.socket — would therefore have changed NOTHING and passed for the wrong reason. That is the failure SUBSTRATE.md 5 names and that has already happened twice here. Caught by checking what actually owns the name before writing the control.

TWO HERMETIC CONTROLS ATTEMPTED AND ABANDONED rather than written up as successes: a session bus with XDG_DATA_DIRS pointed away still resolved the service and hung on discover_other_daemon; a private dbus-daemon with no service directories did not answer at all. Short of removing the package the failing path is not reproducible here, and the record says so.

VERSION REGEX BUG CAUGHT BEFORE IT LANDED. pacman -Q prints 'gnome-keyring 1:50.0-1.1'. The regex every other record uses, ([0-9][0-9.]*), matches the EPOCH and reports the version as '1'. This is the first record here carrying a pacman epoch. Fixed to (?:[0-9]+:)?([0-9][0-9.]*), which captures 50.0. Found by running the regex against the real output instead of assuming its shape.

presence and check genuinely disagree usefully here, which is the clearest case on the machine for q4r's distinction: pacman -Q answers 'is the package there', the busctl call answers 'is the service alive'. Uninstalled reads 'not installed' and fails the run; installed-but-dead reads 'installed but not answering'.

ms status: 'gnome-keyring 50.0 secret service answers', rc 0. ms changes detected the transaction as 2 packages, gnome-keyring plus its gcr 3.41.2-2.1 dependency; recorded. 33/33 acceptance, 44/44 cap, 11/11 machine.

PAM AUTO-UNLOCK NOT TAKEN. Drafted in machine-state-t0u.10.md section 3 with the exact file, the two optional lines and their required ordering. /etc/pam.d/greetd is untouched. Recorded there and in the tooling record: the file is owned by the greetd package AND was already edited once by noctalia, which left greetd.bak.noctalia.20260830145901 beside it, so a future noctalia run can revert our lines and the failure would be quiet — login keeps working, the keyring just prompts again.
close_reason: Secret Service exists and answers; record written with an honest falsifiability section. PAM auto-unlock deliberately left drafted and untaken.

Prefer the ASUS-Linux/OpenGamingCollective asusctl stack over generic RGB probing. Keep lighting control separate from fan curves, TDP, battery charging, GPU switching, and other Armoury controls unless those are explicitly scoped later.
design: Primary candidate: CachyOS-packaged asusctl/asusd, optionally followed by rog-control-center only if the CLI is insufficient. Current local repository evidence on 2026-09-03: signed CachyOS asusctl 6.4.0-1, 7.10 MiB download and 26.55 MiB installed; signed rog-control-center 6.4.0-1 is optional. Upstream asusctl added G835L-family support in 6.3.0 and corrected its supported lighting modes in 6.3.1; current releases also include AniMe Vision packet fixes. Confirm package provenance, daemon/udev activation, configuration ownership, persistence, update and uninstall paths, and interaction with firmware/Windows settings. Draft a canonical tooling record and obtain explicit approval before installation or visible changes. Then test brightness, a static low-intensity colour, the chassis light bar, sleep/boot power states, and AniMe Vision independently, preserving a known way to turn every surface off. Determine whether CLI-only control is sufficient before considering rog-control-center. title: ms status resolves record checks through PATH, so a narrow PATH reports present tools as absent
description:
Found while implementing machine-state-an1, 2026-09-03.

A tooling record now declares that the machine should have the tool, and 'ms status' fails when a
recorded tool is absent. Absence is decided by running the record's check command, resolved through
PATH.

Under a narrower PATH than an interactive shell — a systemd timer, a hook, cron — the three tools in
~/.local/bin (beads, claude, dcg) resolve to nothing, so 'ms status' reports them 'recorded here but
not installed' and exits 1. Reproduced with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin: four tools reported absent, three of
them wrongly.

Same class as the bug already fixed in 'ms changes', where loose binaries were re-resolved through
PATH every run and would have been dropped from the inventory then reported as newly appeared. The
fix there was to re-check a known tool at its RECORDED path. 'ms status' has no recorded path to
fall back to, so the fix is not identical.

Harmless today because the SessionStart hook runs 'ms changes', not 'ms status'. It stops being
harmless the moment anything scheduled or hooked runs 'ms status'.
acceptance_criteria:
- ms status reports the same verdicts under a narrow PATH as under an interactive one.
- A genuinely absent tool is still reported absent.
- A negative control proves the discrimination: with the fix disabled, a present tool is reported
  absent under a narrow PATH.
close_reason: Tool paths remembered in state/tooling.json and used when PATH cannot resolve them; genuinely absent tools still absent. Two remaining environment-dependent verdicts (hyprctl needing the compositor session, dcg doctor checking its own PATH presence) are correct behaviour and recorded rather than fixed — the filed acceptance asked for identical verdicts everywhere, which is stronger than is true. 24/24 with a negative control.

title: Define the next application roles and role-specific actions
description: Extend the provisional application-role model using the useful distinction found in Omarchy: a role names an interchangeable workstation responsibility, while verbs and variants are actions on that role. Evaluate an intentionally small next set of durable roles: browser, mail, calendar, terminal, editor, file-manager, password-manager, music, messaging, notes, and AI. Keep products and services such as Docker, YouTube, Maps, Photos, and individual social sites as applications/services or capabilities rather than roles.
design: Preserve normalized role identity separately from its selected implementation and window-matching evidence. The mapping is many-to-many: one application may fulfil several roles, and a role may be reassigned without changing workflows. Model operations such as mail.open, mail.compose, browser.open, browser.open-private, file-manager.open, file-manager.open-at-directory, text-editor.open, code-editor.open-project, and code-editor.open-diff as actions, not additional roles. Split the ambiguous editor role into text-editor for quick arbitrary text editing and code-editor for repositories, language tooling, debugging, and integrated terminals; VS Code, Zed, Cursor, or Neovim may fulfil code-editor, while Neovim may fulfil both. Treat creative work by intent: start with graphics-editor if the real workflow is general visual composition, then split only when necessary into photo-editor, vector-editor, and page-layout. Affinity Photo/Designer/Publisher and Linux alternatives are implementations, not role identities. Omarchy is evidence for vocabulary, not the schema: upstream has configurable defaults for browser, terminal, and editor, a stable file-manager function, and semantic binding labels, but no formal general-purpose role registry. Widen from existing roles only when a real workflow needs each addition.
acceptance_criteria: Document the role-versus-application-versus-action classification. Select the smallest next role justified by a concrete workflow. Add each accepted role through canonical declarations and verify that bindings, previews, agent catalogue, and window resolution remain coherent. Do not create catch-all roles for individual sites or products, and do not expand every candidate merely because it appears in this planning list.
notes: ROLE REFINEMENT 2026-09-03. Applications belong in the implementation registry; roles state why they are opened; actions state what should happen. Do not preserve a generic editor role merely because Omarchy names one. Proposed editing identities are text-editor and code-editor. Proposed creative identities are initially graphics-editor, or workload-specific photo-editor, vector-editor, and page-layout when actual usage justifies the distinction. Avoid a vague creative-app role and avoid prematurely creating all three Affinity-shaped roles. Example many-to-many mapping: Neovim may implement both text-editor and code-editor; VS Code implements code-editor; Krita or GIMP may implement photo-editor; Inkscape may implement vector-editor; Scribus may implement page-layout. The selected programs remain replaceable without renaming human or agent workflows.

title: Run ms changes at session start, so the agent notices without being told
description:
The detection built in machine-state-2zm works, but it only runs when someone asks. If the
agent has to be told 'done' before it looks, the loop is not closed — it is reporting that a human
triggers.

A Claude Code SessionStart hook closes it. Established experimentally 2026-09-03 that this is safe:
bd's claude recipe preserves a foreign SessionStart entry. Proven properly, by DELETING bd's own
entry so bd had to write, then confirming the foreign one survived alongside the one bd added — the
first attempt looked like it passed while bd had not written at all, which would have proved nothing.

Needs a quiet mode: printing 'nothing changed since ...' into context at every session start is
noise that would train the reader to skip it.
acceptance_criteria:
- ms changes --quiet prints nothing when nothing changed, and the change list when something did.
- A SessionStart hook runs it, and does not fail the session when changes are pending.
- bd setup claude still repairs its own hook with ours present.
close_reason: SessionStart hook runs 'ms changes --quiet'; co-tenancy with bd's hook proven by forcing bd to write. Quiet mode prints only when something moved, and never fails the session.

The baseline currently has no node, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, or deno on PATH. Choose a supported Node.js installation and version-management strategy, package-manager policy, TypeScript execution and build tooling, and global-tool policy before installation. title: Add Steam
description: Research and later install Steam as the workstation gaming client. Confirm the appropriate Arch/CachyOS package source and required multilib, graphics, audio, controller, filesystem, and Proton compatibility dependencies before installation. Treat account login and library locations as user-owned state.
design:
PACKAGE: multilib/steam 1.0.0.87-3, Valve's own, packaged by Levente Polyak, SHA-256 and signature validated by pacman. NOT cachyos/steam-jupiter-stable 1.0.0.85-11, which is the Deck/Jupiter bootstrap packaging and is aimed at a handheld session, not a laptop desktop. No AUR helper, no Flatpak — same rule the Proton records follow.

TRANSACTION MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED, on 2026-09-05. 'pacman -Sp --print-format' with stdin closed resolves 26 packages and asks nothing: 14 direct dependencies are missing plus 11 pulled transitively, then steam itself. No provider prompt appears because lib32-nvidia-utils and lib32-vulkan-intel are already installed, so lib32-vulkan-driver and lib32-libgl are already satisfied. That matters here — 'never issue a command that can block on a prompt' is a repository rule, and provider selection is exactly such a prompt. It was checked rather than assumed.

GRAPHICS: Intel Arrow Lake-S iGPU plus NVIDIA RTX 5090 Max-Q, hybrid. Both kernels carry the open modules (linux-cachyos-nvidia-open, linux-cachyos-lts-nvidia-open) and nvidia-prime is installed, so the discrete GPU is reached per-process with 'prime-run', set as a per-game launch option rather than machine-wide. Nothing to install for this.

STORAGE, decided rather than deferred: the Steam default, ~/.local/share/Steam, with no separate library and no separate shader cache. /home is a single 950G filesystem with 938G free; inventing a second library location would create a second place to keep in step for no benefit today. Revisit only when a real capacity problem exists.

VERIFICATION: 'pacman -Qkk steam', which launches nothing. The same reasoning as proton-pass: a check that starts a GUI to prove a package is installed is worse than no check.

AND ITS LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: pacman -Qkk verifies the LAUNCHER only. Steam bootstraps and updates its own runtime, Proton builds and game content under ~/.local/share/Steam, none of it owned by any package and none of it covered by this check. The record must say so. This is the largest body of self-updating third-party code on the machine and pretending one check covers it would be the exact failure these records exist to prevent.

ONE SYSTEM-LEVEL SIDE EFFECT worth naming before approval: the steam-devices dependency installs udev rules under /usr/lib/udev/rules.d granting access to controller hardware. It is the only part of this transaction that changes device permissions.
acceptance_criteria: Package provenance confirmed from multilib with pacman signature validation, and the choice against steam-jupiter-stable recorded with its reason. The install transaction measured and proven prompt-free before any command runs. GPU, multilib, audio, controller and Proton prerequisites reviewed against what is actually installed rather than against a general guide. Library and shader-cache location decided and recorded, not deferred. canonical/tooling/steam.md drafted and reviewable BEFORE installation, carrying a check that launches nothing and an explicit statement of what that check does not cover. title: Refusal wording collapsed unimplemented into unavailable
description:
Found by a keypress, not by a test. SUPER + G is bound to desktop.workspace.arrange, which is
declared and deliberately unimplemented. Pressing it raised a notification titled 'Action
unavailable', and the person who pressed it reported back that the action was unavailable — which is
not what is true.

cap preview had it right all along: the IMPL column read 'missing'. So two surfaces described one
action with two different facts, which is precisely what this slice exists to prevent. The catalogue
distinguishes invalid, unimplemented and runtime-unavailable; refuse() flattened the last two into
one message and one notification title.

The distinction decides what to do next. UNAVAILABLE means the provider exists and something it
needs is not running — start it, or retry. NOT IMPLEMENTED means nothing changes until code is
written and retrying is pointless.

FIXED: a REFUSAL table gives each state its own title and message, cmd_act and cmd_propose pass the
state, and the journal records it — a corpus of bare 'refused' cannot later tell absent code from an
absent desktop. tests 20, 21, 22 with a negative control that restores the shared wording.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each refusal state has its own wording and notification title.
- preview and the runtime refusal name the same state for the same action.
- The journal records which refusal it was.
- A negative control proves the assertion fails when the wording is shared again.
close_reason: Fixed and tested in the same session it was found.

title: Assert the vendor accounting invariant at runtime, not only in a test
description:
From the independent review (machine-state-8cy), finding 8 — accepted as accurate, with one
residual worth closing.

The evidence limit is already recorded in CAPABILITIES.md 5.1: this reads single textual lines
containing hl.bind and resolves a small Lua concatenation grammar. It is not a Lua interpreter and
does not see the runtime keymap.

THE RESIDUAL: the invariant that makes the limit safe — every hl.bind occurrence lands in either
'resolved' or 'unreadable', never neither — is asserted only in tests/cap.py against a fixture. The
live file is not checked against it. A vendor line shaped so the parser matches nothing would be
counted in neither bucket and disappear silently, which is exactly the defect bru.7.4 fixed for a
different shape.

An invariant that protects against unknown future input has to hold on the input, not on a fixture.
acceptance_criteria:
- vendor_bindings asserts its own accounting against the count of hl.bind occurrences in the file.
- A file the parser cannot fully account for fails visibly rather than appearing complete.
- The check runs on the live file, not only in tests.

title: Do not describe propose-first as behaviour until code requires it
description:
From the independent review (machine-state-8cy), finding 2. VERIFIED.

cmd_act reads CAP_CALLER with a default of 'agent' and executes immediately. No proposal, no
approval token, no check of the consequence class. The module constants are honest —
ENFORCEMENT = 'advisory', UNATTENDED_AVAILABLE = False — and the catalogue reports them.

But the comment inside cmd_act, beside the call that executes, reads:

    # A person pressing a key has already expressed intent; an agent proposes
    # first. Same action identity, different authorization context.

That describes a convention as though it were the code's behaviour, sitting next to the code that
does not implement it. Either enforce it or say plainly that it is a convention this code does not
yet require. bru.5 is where enforcement lands.
acceptance_criteria:
- No comment or document describes propose-first as enforced while the code does not require it.
- The convention is still stated, marked clearly as convention.
- ENFORCEMENT and UNATTENDED_AVAILABLE remain the single place enforcement is reported.
close_reason: Convention marked as convention in code and stated explicitly in the agent-facing catalogue (propose_required); three limitations recorded in CAPABILITIES.md 7.1 with their expiry conditions.

title: Validate bindings, roles and invocation arguments as strictly as actions
description:
From the independent review (machine-state-8cy), finding 6. VERIFIED.

actions() validates namespacing, label and consequence, and rejects. key_bindings() and roles() do
neither: they index b['keys'] and b['action'] directly, so a missing key raises a traceback rather
than a diagnosis, and a wrong type fails somewhere later.

Invocation parsing is looser still:

    args = dict(a.split('=', 1) for a in argv[1:] if '=' in a)

A token without '=' is silently DISCARDED. 'cap act desktop.application.ensure mail' looks like it
asks for the mail role and in fact asks for no role at all. Argument names are never checked against
the action's declared arguments, so a typo'd name is accepted and ignored.

Rejecting a malformed declaration is already the established pattern here; this extends it to the
declarations that did not get it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bindings and roles are validated on load with messages naming the file and the problem.
- A token without '=' is an error, not a silent discard.
- Argument names are validated against the action declaration.
- Tests cover each malformed shape.
close_reason: Roles, bindings and invocation arguments validated on load and at call time; bare tokens and unknown argument names rejected; usage errors kept out of the journal; dangling role references caught where dangling actions are. 37/37 cap, 13/13 acceptance.

title: Experience cohesion: plan as a sibling epic once bru proves the vocabulary
description:
Placeholder holding a design review's conclusion so it is not lost. NOT yet an epic, deliberately.

THE GAP: machine-state governs state and machine-state-bru will govern runtime action, but neither
gives the workstation one vocabulary. Today a key could run a shell command, a Noctalia menu could
carry a third name for the same operation, and a shortcut preview could document a binding that no
longer exists — all working independently while the system as a whole misinforms its user.

THE PROPOSED LAYER: one semantic theme from which application themes derive; one keybinding
registry from which both live bindings and their preview derive; one action vocabulary shared by
keys, menus, agents, notifications and events; one application-role registry so workflows target
mail rather than proton-mail; and one account of which bindings are ours, a vendor's, or in
conflict — the binding equivalent of CANONICAL, VENDOR and PROJECTED.

THE SEAM: a stable namespaced action identifier. A key binding, a menu entry, an agent call and an
event binding all name desktop.application.open. The experience layer decides where an action
appears; the broker decides whether and how it may run. Neither assumes the other's authority.

WHY IT IS A SIBLING AND NOT A PHASE: cohesion spans durable state and runtime action; the broker is
deliberately runtime-only. Its declarations are canonical state projected by ms; it references
capability names but owns none.

WHY NOT YET, three reasons, all grounded:
  1. It would be planned against capability identifiers that do not exist until bru phases 1 and 2.
  2. Theme work is blocked behind machine-state-a22. Noctalia already owns cross-application
     theming here — 54 templates, live theme files in six applications — and projecting a canonical
     theme into them would start a rewrite war over settings nobody here has an opinion about.
  3. binds.lua declares 75 bindings and is byte-identical to the CachyOS template. Zero are ours.
     A keybinding registry would begin by describing vendor state, not owning it, which is a more
     modest and more honest claim than generating a keymap.

The full review is machine-state-bru.md at repository root.
acceptance_criteria:
- Opened as an epic only after bru phases 1 and 2 are complete and machine-state-a22 is decided.
- The first vertical slice is deliberately small: one token set, two targets, one binding, one preview, one role.
- Key bindings and event bindings keep distinct schemas and loaders.

title: Grant loading and enforcement at invocation
description:
SHARED CONTEXT (true for every bead in this epic)

The tool is a PEER to bin/ms and must never be folded into it. ms governs durable projection and
drift; this governs runtime capabilities and actions. Folding them gives the projector a runtime
and the runtime the projector's write access. Read SUBSTRATE.md and CAPABILITIES.md in this

  by disabling the guard.

  this repository.

Grants become live. Until this bead, they govern nothing.

ESTABLISHED FACTS about the boundary, from machine-state-u40:
grants live at /etc/machine-state/grants.toml, root-owned, and the containing directory must be
root-owned too because deleting a file needs write permission on its directory rather than the
file. sudo requires a password on this machine, verified, which is what makes root a real boundary.

a boundary. bin/ms already verifies this boundary and exits non-zero if it is compromised.

FAIL-CLOSED: absent, unreadable or malformed grants means nothing runs unattended. Absence is the
correct initial state, not a degraded one.

EXPECT THE SCHEMA TO BE WRONG. It was designed against zero capabilities. Revise it deliberately
now that real capabilities exist, and record what changed and why.

- A capability runs unattended only with a matching grant.
- Absent, unreadable or malformed grants results in nothing running unattended.
- Any schema revision is recorded with the reason.
- The existing boundary verification in bin/ms still passes.
